Sam: Quick results from last night's MB sweep (streaming chat vs non-streaming completions). TL;DR: mb=4 keeps p99s in check for streaming, but completions throughput keeps improving up to mb=32/64 with p95 tradeoffs.

Priya: perf-bot dump attached below — ran two workloads: chat_stream (avg len 80, user typing pattern) and bulk_completions (batch gen, seq len 512).

perf-bot: `run --suite=mb-sweep --models=redwood-v1 --nodes=gpu-pool-a --runs=3`

```
# chat_stream (seq 80):
mb=2  p50=18ms  p95=62ms  p99=92ms  tok/s=1250  kv_hit=0.86  kernel=fused-attn-v2
mb=4  p50=22ms  p95=58ms  p99=78ms  tok/s=1400  kv_hit=0.85  kernel=fused-attn-v2
mb=8  p50=30ms  p95=85ms  p99=180ms tok/s=1550  kv_hit=0.73  kernel=matmul-stream (tail)

# bulk_completions (seq 512):
mb=8  p50=45ms  p95=150ms p99=260ms tok/s=4200  kv_hit=0.60  kernel=matmul-batched
mb=32 p50=70ms  p95=220ms p99=550ms tok/s=6100  kv_hit=0.48  kernel=matmul-batched
mb=64 p50=110ms p95=330ms p99=900ms tok/s=7400  kv_hit=0.35  kernel=matmul-batched
```

Miguel: Noticed the big p99 jump at mb>=8 for chat_stream — kernel switch to `matmul-stream` + KV hit drop looks correlated. My hypothesis: larger microbatches increase kv cache churn (more unique contexts merged), causing more KV evictions and fallback to a slower kernel path for tail shards.

Cassie: Added a couple of logs from the run where we saw eviction spikes around mb=8: `kv_evictions=1.8/s -> 5.6/s` and `tail_latency_spike at 2026-11-03T03:12Z`. Those correlate with background GC on the allocator (we saw small pausing).

Sam: So actionable summary: for streaming chat we should bias towards mb<=4 to keep p99 low. For non-streaming bulk completions, larger mb boosts throughput but at cost of long tails — acceptable for some customers but bad for interactive.

Priya: Suggest two immediate experiments before we change defaults: 1) enable kernel hinting so short-seq chat routes to fused-attn even if mb is larger (force kernel selection when seq<=128). 2) try hybrid MB policy: route streaming endpoints to mb=4 with aggressive prefix caching; route batch endpoints to mb=32 with prefetching.

Miguel: For (1) I ran a quick patch that exposes `kernel_hint: prefer_fused_for_short_seq` — results look promising (keeps p99 ~85ms at mb=8) but KV hit stayed low. Means kernel hint reduces compute fallback but doesn't fix cache churn.

Priya: Code snippet for the hybrid policy config we propose to test:
```
routes:
  - name: streaming-chat
    mb_target: 4
    kernel_hint: prefer_fused_for_short_seq
    kv_prefetch: handshake-prefix
  - name: batch-completions
    mb_target: 32
    kv_prefetch: aggressive
    allow_slow_tail: true
```

Cassie: Another angle: increase KV capacity (temp) or tune eviction threshold to keep hit rates up for mb>=8. That will reduce p99 but increase memory cost. Worth A/Bing for high-SLA customers.

Sam: Next steps: Priya + Miguel to run 48h A/B with kernel-hint + hybrid policy on us-east1 pool. Cassie to run KV-capacity bump experiment on a 2-node slice and measure mem/cost. I'll coordinate rollback windows.

Priya: I'll kick off the runs this afternoon and tag the canary with `canary/mb-hybrid-20261103`. Expect initial numbers in 12-18h.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary/mb-hybrid-20261103 -> gpu-pool-a at 2026-11-03T16:00Z :rocket: (will notify on completion).

Miguel: One more note — we should capture per-token kernel selection traces in the profiler (add `trace_kernel=true`) so we can quantify how often the fallback path hits under mixed workloads.

Sam: Agreed. Add that to the run plan. Good work team :thumbsup:
